sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in Denison
sections.html:
A Denison's owner can hire an agent, hunt for a buyer alone, or phone someone who pays cash. Speed, repair spending and the final price all pull in different directions, so decide your priorities before you pick up any call.

Denison grew up around the railroad. The city was established on September 23, 1872, and incorporated on March 7, 1873. It sits in Grayson County and has roughly 28,000 residents. In a smaller city the pool of listing buyers is thinner, and a house with deferred maintenance can sit longer than it would in a big metro.

  • On the market: a stronger price is possible, but you face open houses, inspection requests and loan approval.
  • By owner: the commission is yours to keep, along with every contract and every round of haggling.
  • To a cash buyer: few contingencies and an early closing, with a price that has the buyer's repair costs built in.

sections.h2: Who bills Denison property tax, and the 2025 rates
sections.html:
Bills come from the Grayson County Tax Assessor-Collector. Value is the job of the Grayson County Appraisal District, found at 205 N Travis Street in Sherman. The county tax office has a main location at 100 W Houston in Sherman and a Denison office at the County Sub-Courthouse, 101 W Woodard.

Rates per $100 of value, 2025 tax year
Taxing unitRate per $100 of value
City of Denison0.712034
Denison Independent School District1.155000
Grayson County0.305100
Grayson College0.145980
Total combined rate2.318114

Sales tax is 8.25 percent and the hotel and motel tax is 7 percent. Your own bill may differ from this table, so call the county tax office to confirm. For general city questions, the administration offices are at 300 W. Main St.

Tax notices arrive in October and payment is normally due by January 31. A bill still open on February 1 is delinquent, and from then on the collector adds penalty and interest, with the penalty rising until July 1. The year's lien lands on January 1 on whoever owns the house, which is why buyers and title companies insist the current year be settled when you close.

  • Call the Grayson County tax office early for the balance on your account.
  • State law lets owners who are over 65 or disabled pay in four installments.
  • A delinquent account may qualify for a payment plan, which a homestead owner can insist on.

If you owe back taxes, the title company can pay them from your sale proceeds when it closes the file.

sections.h2: Permits to sort out before you hand over the house
sections.html:
Most structural work needs a city permit, and a few of the ones sellers forget are worth checking. A permit is required for any new fence, a replacement fence, or a fence repair covering 20 feet or more, and for every detached storage building or shed of any size.

A building permit stays valid while work goes on. It expires if work is suspended or abandoned for 180 days after issue or after the last approved inspection. An owner can take out a homeowner permit only for an owner-occupied single-family house that carries a homestead exemption, which the appraisal district verifies. A rental or a house without the exemption sends the applicant down the general contractor route, and any electrical, plumbing or mechanical work that needs a state license stays off limits.

The application usually asks for a scope of work with materials, owner and contractor contact details, a site plan or drawing, and a registered contractor. Request a final inspection through the online portal. The building office keeps weekday hours, 8 am to 5 pm. Cash or check works for in-person permit payments at the Building Inspections office, and the portal takes cards.

One part of town has extra rules. In the area running from the 700 block of West Main to the 300 block of East Main, between Gandy Street and Crawford Street, exterior work, including painting, goes to the Historical Preservation Board. A buyer planning changes there should ask the city first. Certificates of occupancy apply to new buildings and tenant spaces, so the owner of a mixed-use building downtown should ask the department which rule fits.

Texas sets fixed steps for both situations, and a quick sale can work in either one if the paperwork is ready. If the owner left a will, there is a four-year window to probate it. If there is no will and the estate is small, a small estate affidavit can fit. It covers $75,000 in assets, leaves out homestead and exempt property, and needs a court's approval.

When a mortgage is in default, the lender mails a default notice, and paying the missed amount within 20 days reinstates the loan. A public sale follows an auction notice and happens on a first Tuesday, within a set window from morning to afternoon. Ask the Grayson County clerk where foreclosure notices are posted.

If you close before the sale date, the foreclosure on that loan stops. Have your servicer put the payoff in writing.

A notary witnesses your signature, and the Grayson County clerk, who keeps the land records, files the deed. A conveyance without a proper acknowledgment cannot be recorded. Even though a branch tax office sits in town, a Denison house is filed in Grayson County, the county of the land. The title company will quote the clerk's recording charges and the final total.

Before you list, gather the last deed, your tax receipts and any lien releases. One missing paper can hold up a closing.

Accepting an offer starts a paper chase. Ask your lender for a payoff, get the current balance from the tax office, and confirm that every fence, shed or remodel permit has been closed out. If a tenant or a relative lives in the house, agree the move-out date in writing. Walk the property once more before closing, and take out anything the contract says you will remove.

Keep copies of what you send to the title company, and note the date. If a buyer asks for a repair credit or a later closing, answer in writing so the contract and your records match. A short written summary of the terms you agreed, sent to the buyer and the title company, heads off most late disputes.

A cash closing usually moves faster than a financed one, since no lender has to approve anything. On either route, try to see the settlement statement a day ahead, and have the title company explain any charge that looks unfamiliar.

faqs.q: Which county handles taxes on a house in Denison?
faqs.a: Grayson County. The county Tax Assessor-Collector bills you, while the Grayson County Appraisal District decides the value.

faqs.q: Does Denison tell homeowners the total tax rate?
faqs.a: Yes. The combined rate for the 2025 tax year is 2.318114, made up of the city, school district, county and college rates. Your own bill may differ, so ask the county tax office.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for a shed or fence in Denison?
faqs.a: Yes for a shed of any size, and for a new fence or a repair covering 20 feet or more. The city asks for a site plan with dimensions from the property lines.

faqs.q: When does a Texas tax bill go delinquent?
faqs.a: On February 1, for taxes not paid by January 31. Penalty and interest start to accrue at that point.

faqs.q: Is probate always required to sell an inherited Denison house?
faqs.a: Not always. Options include a small estate affidavit, a muniment of title or an affidavit of heirship, and the title company decides which it will accept. The Grayson County clerk can say what must be filed.
